title: Own one vehicle in the off-road benchmark
why: The off-road targets have to be justified against at least three production vehicles, using public specifications.
output: One fully sourced row in the benchmark sheet for your vehicle: suspension, ground clearance, approach, breakover and departure angles, wheelbase, turning radius, driveline, underbody protection and recovery points.
done_when: Every cell holds a value or a clearly marked gap, and every value has a public source.

title: Own one line of the vehicle target table
why: Year 1 asks for a target range on each vehicle requirement, with the reasoning behind it.
output: One requirement written as a measurable target: value, unit, source, rationale and how it will be verified.
done_when: A lead who did not write it can tell how the target would be tested.
source: Vehicle Design Rules, vehicle technical specification

title: Own one candidate in the rear drive unit benchmark
why: The team has to compare electric drive units before it can choose one, and every number needs a source.
output: One sourced row for a candidate drive unit: power, torque, mass, size, voltage and cooling.
done_when: Every value has a source, and missing values are marked as gaps instead of guessed.
source: Year 1 taskline: rear eAxle benchmark and packaging

title: Own one row of the mass budget
why: Everything the team adds has to fit inside one weight allowance, so each added part needs an owner and a sourced mass.
output: One mass budget row for a component: mass, source, and your name as its owner.
done_when: The row has a source for its number and is reviewed by the Vehicle Track Technical Lead.

title: Follow the CAD onboarding guide as a first-time user
why: The guide is part of a graded submission, and it only works if someone new can follow it without help.
output: A short list of every step that was unclear or failed, handed to the guide's authors.
done_when: You reached the end of the guide, or recorded exactly where you could not continue.

title: Own one signal group in the measurement plan
why: Baseline testing needs a list of what to measure before any test is planned.
output: Rows in the signal list for one group of signals: name, unit, where it is measured and which test needs it.
done_when: Each signal has a unit and a named test that uses it.
capacity: Several owners - one signal group each

title: Write the bench CAN setup so the next person can repeat it
why: Getting a CAN adapter to show its first frame on the bench takes hours the first time and minutes once it is written down.
output: A one-page bench setup note: adapter, software, bit rate, connector pinout and termination, with a screenshot of received frames.
done_when: A second member follows the note and sees frames without asking for help.

title: Follow the controls onboarding guide end to end
why: This guide is the whole of a graded submission, so it has to work for a real new member.
output: A list of every step that was unclear or failed, with the error message where there was one.
done_when: The virtual vehicle model opens and runs on your machine, or the blocking step is recorded.

title: Own one drive cycle run of the virtual vehicle
why: The simulation report compares the model against published figures on three standard drive cycles.
output: A saved run of one cycle (UDDS, HWFET or US06) with a labelled plot and the change in battery state of charge recorded.
done_when: Another member reproduces your result from your notes.

title: Build one small Simulink model for your subsystem
why: A model of five to eight blocks teaches the pattern the full vehicle model is built from.
output: One small model, a script holding its parameters, one plot, and the answer to the question the model was built for.
done_when: The model runs from the script alone and the plot is labelled with units.

title: Own one pack configuration in the sweep
why: The battery targets need several series and parallel arrangements checked against the same limits.
output: One configuration worked through: pack voltage, energy, module voltage and per-cell current, each checked against the competition limits.
done_when: The arithmetic is shown, units are stated, and a second member has checked it.

title: Write the contactor and precharge sequence on paper
why: The battery disconnect unit needs its states and fault cases written down before anything is built.
output: A state table for the sequence (open, precharge, closed, fault) and a list of fault cases to test. Analysis and modelling only - no work on energized hardware.
done_when: Each state has an entry condition and an exit condition, and each fault case names the expected response.
capacity: Several owners - one fault group each
source: Battery disconnect unit and HV safety work

title: Become the scorecard watcher
why: Each scorecard is released about a month before its deliverable is due, and it defines what is graded.
output: For each new scorecard: a checklist of the graded items, handed to the deliverable's owner the week it appears.
done_when: The owner confirms the checklist matches the scorecard.

title: Map the dependencies for one swimlane
why: The Year 1 workplan needs to show which work is waiting on which, and where classes collide with deadlines.
output: A dependency map for one swimlane: what each task needs first, who provides it, and the top schedule risks.
done_when: The swimlane lead agrees the map is right.

title: Keep the outreach log
why: Outreach and social media activity are submitted at the end of the year and cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
output: A running log of every outreach event and post: date, audience, what happened, and a photo where there is one.
done_when: The log is current at each Friday meeting.
source: Social Media Data, Outreach Data and Asset Library requirement

title: Run one customer interview
why: The innovation track is judged on what real customers said, not on what the team assumes.
output: Notes from one interview against the shared question guide, with the three things you did not expect.
done_when: The Product Innovation Track lead has the notes and the interview is counted.
